Single Responsibility — Spec is focused on one concern: preventing noop reruns after gate-impl FAIL.; Unambiguous Requirements — Requirements are concrete and mostly verifiable (specific triggers, fields, errors, and behaviors).; Complete Context — Each requirement includes a condition (When/If) and an expected shall/shall not outcome.; No Hardcoded Secrets — No API keys, passwords, tokens, or secret literals are present in the content.; No Silent Error Swallowing — Error handling is explicit; rejection path requires throwing NO_PROGRESS_SINCE_LAST_FAIL.; Prioritize Requirements — There are more than three requirements (REQ-1..REQ-8) but no explicit priority order is defined.; Impact on Existing Features — Impact is described via scope/out-of-scope and phase targeting, including unaffected gates.; Bounded Resource Usage — Retry behavior is bounded by an explicit ceiling and no unbounded recursion/retry loop is introduced.; Changes Require Test Coverage — Acceptance criteria and test strategy include happy-path and key behavioral tests for the change.; Spec Includes Test Strategy — A dedicated Test Strategy section specifies what to test and how.; Synthesize Draft, Do Not Copy — Cannot verify whether text was synthesized vs copied without the original draft source.; Record Unresolved Points as Open Questions — Open Questions is explicitly present and marked none; unresolved items are not hidden.; Include 'Why This Approach' Rationale — Rationale is provided through background, design principles, and alternatives considered with rejection reasons.; Do Not Modify Existing Tests Without Approval — Spec proposes adding new tests and does not state modifying/deleting existing tests.; Backward-Compatible CLI Interface — No command/option removal or semantic change requiring CLI migration steps is specified.; Exit Code Contract — Spec explicitly requires non-zero exit behavior on failure/rejection paths.
